headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from shared file-based workflows; no direct evidence of a dangerous default bridge.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman reads and writes project files like CLAUDE.md, memory files, and project notes, while great_expectations consumes data sources and validation results. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content in caveman influence what great_expectations treats as input. No direct bridge is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory
IF caveman writes attacker-controlled instructions into files that great_expectations later reads
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Require manual review before great_expectations reads caveman-authored files
Add a filename allowlist for shared inputs
Strip instruction-like text from handoff files
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch files, and caveman explicitly handles session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md while great_expectations reads data sources and writes validation results. That creates a plausible shared-workspace leakage path for sensitive project data, even though both profiles show network_egress:none. The lack of direct isolation evidence keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF the agents share a filesystem or mounted workspace
IF caveman stores sensitive notes or logs in files that great_expectations can read
mitigations: Use separate workspaces per agent
Move sensitive notes out of shared paths
Restrict file permissions on logs and memory files
Review validation outputs before sharing them back
requires-engineering: enforce workspace sandboxing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and uses MCP plus file surfaces, while great_expectations can install packages and works on data files. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource or shared OAuth scopes, so a direct capability conflict is not established. The plausible conflict is limited to unusual shared-directory setups.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory
IF package installation or file edits target the same mutable project state
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time
Assign separate output directories
Lock shared files during edits
Keep package installs isolated from data work
requires-engineering: add resource locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman can generate project notes and CLAUDE.md content, and great_expectations produces validation results that may be treated as authoritative downstream. If great_expectations consumes caveman output without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into incorrect data-quality decisions. The profiles do not prove an automated handoff, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF great_expectations ingests caveman-authored notes or configs as authoritative input
IF no human or automated verification step checks the handoff
mitigations: Require a validation step before acting on caveman output
Compare outputs against source data
Flag low-confidence claims for review
Keep generated notes separate from executable configs
requires-engineering: add schema validation on handoff files

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source, docs-only, and show no secrets, OAuth scopes, or regulated data classes like PHI or EU PII. caveman touches session logs and memory files, but the profiles do not indicate a residency or certification mismatch with great_expectations. This is a low compliance concern because only generic logging/retention ambiguity is visible.
conditions: IF regulated data is later stored in caveman session logs or memory files
IF great_expectations validation results are retained under a stricter policy than caveman logs
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared logs
Set short retention for session artifacts
Document which files may contain sensitive data
Review deletion procedures for generated outputs
requires-engineering: align retention policies
